paragraphs.text: This [red tea](red:definition) comes from [Yuchi](yuchi:where-it-is), the township that holds Sun Moon Lake in the middle of Nantou County. Red tea took root here under Japanese rule. Large leaf [Assam](yuchi:assam-planting) seed brought from India did well in the township's trial plantings, because the warm, wet and misty basin, with its deep reddish soil, [reminded the trade of Assam country](yuchi:why-red-tea).

The leaf was made in 1981, when the township's red tea was [fading as an export crop](yuchi:decline-and-return). From the 1970s, rising wages made hand picked leaf expensive next to red tea from other countries, and many growers moved to oolong or to other crops. The revival came only after the 1999 earthquake, so this tea comes from the lean years before it.
Red tea has [no tradition of ageing](red:ageing). It is made to drink within a few years of sealing, and this one is now forty-five years past its making, far beyond the life the style plans for.

brewing.text: Red tea takes water near the boil, about 90 to 100°C; hotter water draws out its aroma and flavour more fully, but its bitterness faster too. In a pot or mug, use about a rounded spoon of leaf for each cup and steep three to five minutes, less for broken leaf and a little less, and a little cooler, for a light, delicate tea. Left too long, it turns bitter and drying, because time and heat pull more tannins from the leaf.

notice.text: A sweet cup, often with honey, floral or fruity notes, malt in many, and a brisk strength in the stronger teas. The liquor runs red, bright to deep.
